newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks renew gains on EU stability deal.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks renew gains on EU stability deal.

text.p: MADRID, June 17 (Reuter) 0830 GMT - Madrid stocks opened higher on Tuesday after a brief slippage late on Monday, renewing an upward trend on an European Union summit agreement in Amsterdam on a key budget stability pact, dealers said.

"The news of Amsterdam has given a new upward push to the bourse despite, it seems, that the euro will not be as strong as originally hoped," one dealer said. * General index rose 2.40 points, 0.41 percent, to 580.78 * Ibex-35 gained 42.28 points, 0.64 percent, to 6,669.48 * Fosforera shares sank the maximum 15 percent to 294 after they started trading again after a suspension

Dealers said a strong bond market was also pushing up stock prices. They said the upward trend was supported by higher than usual trade volume and should continue in a bullish tone on ongoing positive domestic economic news.
Bright prospects in the economy was helping materials producers in particular with heavy trade in Ercros, Sniace, Lain and Tubacex.

Telefonica was up initially then backed off 15 pesetas to 4,315 at 0900 GMT after news late on Monday that Caja Madrid invested 100 billion pesetas in the last three months to get three percent of the operator.
